'''Astrid an Huef''' is a German-born New Zealand mathematician who holds a professorship at [[Victoria University of Wellington]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.victoria.ac.nz/sms/about/staff|title=VUW Maths Department Staff|date=14 June 2024 }}</ref> Until 2017, she held the Chair of Pure Mathematics at the [[University of Otago]]. Her research interests include [[functional analysis]], [[operator algebra]]s, and [[dynamical system]]s,{{r|staff}} particularly operator algebras associated with dynamical systems. She was the president of the [[New Zealand Mathematical Society]] for the 2016–2017 term.{{r|nzms|nzms-admin}}

==Education and career==
An Huef was born in [[Karlsruhe]] and lived in New Zealand for two years as a teenager before moving to Australia in 1985. Because of the disruption to her education caused by these international moves, she was advised not to take higher mathematics in high school, but did so anyway. She began her undergraduate studies in [[computer science]] at the [[University of Newcastle (Australia)|University of Newcastle]], but ended up doing a double degree, with honours in mathematics. While there, she met [[Dartmouth College]] professor Dana Williams, who became her doctoral advisor at Dartmouth beginning in 1994.{{r|nzms}} She completed her doctorate in 1999.{{r|nzms|mgp}} She has collaborated with mathematicians internationally on research related to C algebras and mathematical structures connected to dynamical systems.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Grant |first=Lenette |date=April 2010 |title=NEW COLLEAGUES |url=https://nzmathsoc.org.nz/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/NZMSnews108_Apr2010.pdf? |journal=Newsletter of the New Zealand Mathematical Society |issue=108 |pages=Page 24}}</ref>

She took a tenure track position at the [[University of Denver]], and then worked at the [[University of New South Wales]] for eight years, before being given the chair at Otago in 2008.{{r|nzms}} She currently coordinates the Women in Mathematics community of the New Zealand Mathematical Society.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nzmathsoc.org.nz/?wim|title=Association of women in mathematics nz}}</ref>

In 2019, An Huef was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of New Zealand]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.royalsociety.org.nz/news/researchers-and-scholars-at-the-top-of-their-fields-elected-as-fellows |title=Researchers and scholars at the top of their fields elected as Fellows |date=21 November 2019 |publisher=Royal Society Te Apārangi |accessdate=27 November 2019}}</ref> Te Apārangi in recognition of her contributions to mathematical research.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Statistics |first=Victoria University of Wellington Faculty of Science School of Mathematics and |date=2019-11-28 |title=Prof Astrid An Huef made Fellow of Royal Society Te Apārangi {{!}} Te Kura Mātai Tatauranga / School of Mathematics and Statistics {{!}} Te Herenga Waka |url=https://www.wgtn.ac.nz/sms/about/news/1789606-prof-astrid-an-huef-made-fellow-of-royal-society-te-aparangi |access-date=2026-03-16 |website=Victoria University of Wellington |language=en}}</ref>
